newsitem.title: YEMEN: Dredging in Yemen's Aden port to begin on April 7.
newsitem.headline: Dredging in Yemen's Aden port to begin on April 7.

text.p: Dredging in Aden harbour is due to begin on April 7, the first step towards reviving the port and developing the Aden Free Zone, a zone official said on Saturday.
"The dredging in the port will start on April 7," Dirhim Abdu Numan, president of the Free Zone Authority, told Reuters.
The first support vessel for the dredging project arrived in the port on Saturday and the rest of the equipment was due to arrive in the first week of April, harbour officials said.
The Aden port project is an important element of the Aden Free Zone, a $500 million scheme to make Yemen's economic and commercial capital a major cargo trans-shipment hub.
Officials said earlier this month it would take 15 weeks to scoop out sufficient seabed sand to enable the world's largest container carriers to call.

Aden aims to deepen its navigation channel to 16 metres (52 feet) from a maximum of 12 metres now so it can offer facilities and fast turnaround times for the largest carriers plying shipping routes from Europe through the Suez Canal and the Red Sea to southeast Asia, Australia and East Africa.
